covenants.name: Three Lakes
covenants.summary:
The guiding covenant of the Tribunal, where it meets: its political heavyweights shore up Leczyca in Poland, its Quaesitores turn back the Rhine's and Transylvania's claims, and it keeps the Tribunal's Redcaps. Its device is a golden sunburst in a triangle of three blue ovals.

To its neighbours it is the home of a prosperous trading family, the Beslavichi: old Yury Beslav the patriarch and his son Georgi, who runs the trade, both Gently Gifted Jerbiton magi. Reindeer herds, sleds and carts carry its trade across north Russia and the Baltic, and it has grown rich and well connected by it.

A wooden stockade holds three parts: the Trade Yard of warehouses, reindeer stables and sled yard; the High House with its Great Hall, for specialists, favoured grogs and guests; and the stone Keep above, with the library, treasury and the magi's quarters. A Hermes Portal joins it to Leczyca.

Customs. Its magi have three grades: Juniors, probationers who surrender their sigils and have no voice; Specialists, full members who give up voting and office for research, owing a season a year of teaching or writing; and Seniors, who carry the covenant's duties and alone vote. Up to three magi are away at a time.

Late Autumn. At its bicentenary in 1212 the magi found no apprentice had passed a Gauntlet there in thirty-five years; Boris, at seventy-six, is the youngest by fifteen. Four apprentices have been taken since and are trained by the covenant together, all year round: Mina Dankovna (Yury's), Ratibor Peslav (Zashya's), Dankya Yostovna (Susan's) and Kassim ibn Fadal of Great Bulgar (Olga's). On Thousand Caves the covenant is divided, excited and afraid at once.

covenants.name: Thousand Caves
covenants.summary:
A covenant in the caves of a gorge on the western Urals, its device a labyrinth, and the head of a small confederation of pagan tribes: the valley folk farm, herd, hunt and fish, while bands in the forests about live by hunting, trapping and slash-and-burn, using almost no metal and killing nothing needlessly. The magi are the clan's acknowledged leaders and have deepened the old Slavic bonds with the local beasts and faeries, so that the covenant is ringed by friends. Its people live with late iron-age tools; a good sword is a great prize.

Heart-beasts. Nearly thirty of its folk have avian heart-beasts and thirty more other beasts, which the Bjornaer think the strong Slavic aura has quickened; Nastassia has led the search for them.

The great work. The covenant admits Volkhvy, affiliated to Ex Miscellanea and taught Hermetic magic, and follows Malincka's reasoning that tempering an aura needs three things: a Hermetic Great Ritual, which she is making; the willing part of many mundanes, which its people will give; and a great faerie 'divinity' to bless it. For thirty years the magi have preached a revived cult of Hermes, with festivals and rites and idols in the Great Cavern's sanctum, hoping to bring Hermes back as that god. Lately there are surges of magic and ecstatic dreams, and a Gifted girl, Stenya Vassanovna, Lelya's stepdaughter, says she talks with Lord Hermes and preaches him persuasively.

The book leaves open whether Malincka succeeds (p. 120): reconciliation of the two magics; success with a Hermes who has his own agenda; a partial success that splits the Tribunal; the Slavic gods roused against her; a demon in the god's place; Mongol shamans who destroy the covenant after 1223; or a religion Hermetic theory can never grasp.

covenants.name: Pripet Maior
covenants.summary:
The oldest covenant of the Tribunal, founded by Transylvania and home of House Bjornaer's strongest bond in the east: twice a refuge for Grand Silesia's magi, many of whom stayed. Its device is a house on stilts above a reed bed. In its Autumn, about 1110 to 1165, it was second only to Crintera in the House, and its Roslav Lavickovich was Primus for almost thirty years from 1147. Crintera would still help it in a crisis.

Now it is in Late Winter. Its founders are dead or lost to Final Twilight; its five magi, most of them Stolitzya's old apprentices, range from old and feeble to one step from Final Twilight, sinking into their beasts and into senility. No apprentice in eighty-five years, no new member in seventy. They have given up scholarship and curiosity and spend their lore on defending the marsh. Three or four still attend the Tribunal, whose meetings they gave up to Three Lakes forty years ago.

The island's living palaces rot. Supplies came from the marsh and the rest was bought; now the magi and covenfolk steal what they need, and the vis harvests dwindle because no one makes the effort. Beasts and faeries shun the covenant, the marsh peasants fear and hate it, and much of the trappers', iron-dredgers' and fishers' misfortune is indeed its doing. The Boyar Mikhail of Turov means to dig canals, drain the land, and deal firmly with whoever objects.

covenants.name: Leczyca
covenants.summary:
A strong, well-built castle on its ridge, with a large outer bailey, stables and a tilting run; its device is a quill, point up, with a sword's hilt. Founded by Grand Silesia's survivors, it is the Tribunal's only covenant in Poland and the most at odds with the older Tribunals.

Its powerful turb is trained to harry Rhine interlopers, and it is always ready for siege: it has outlasted more than one Wizard's War. Its outlook is Poland's toward the Germans: it was the Germans who betrayed the Order in the Schism War and squandered their vis, yet they call innocent Leczyca treacherous. The quarrel came with Grand Silesia's desertion of the Rhine, and Durenmar has never forgiven it: at every Grand Tribunal it moves to reassess the eastern border. Crintera and Irencillia have made their peace. Three Lakes counts Leczyca its first line of defence and keeps the Hermes Portal open to it.

Indifferent to Thousand Caves, Leczyca most resents the Royal Embargo: it feels for the Polish nobles, and about 1190 paid a heavy fine for helping Silesian nobles against German raids. Merchant contacts bring it news of roads and armies and a share in their ventures. Its argumentative magi are held together by the enemy outside. Kasina and Frania released their last apprentices two years ago; Ruprecht's apprentice Janek is the only one there now. The Yannes Discourse is kept in its library.

tribunals.name: The Novgorod Tribunal
tribunals.summary:
The Order's Tribunal of the Russian principalities and the Kingdom of Poland, from Novgorod and the northern lakes to Galicia and the steppe, and from Silesia to the Urals. It is young, barely two centuries old, and small: six covenants in a vast land of forest, marsh and river, where faerie vis is rich and the faeries dangerous, and where the Volkhvy, the Slavs' pagan priest-wizards, kept the Order out until the princes turned Christian.

Its founders were three covenants sponsored by Thebes, the Rhine and Transylvania, which refused to fight one another in the Schism War, on the urging of the Hibernian quaesitor Patrick of Dunderry, and made themselves the New Slavonic Tribunal in 1008; it took the name of Novgorod in 1053. Patrick is still its patron saint. Since then it has grown slowly, ejecting foreign magi from its lands, keeping away from the princes, and holding off the Rhine's claim to Poland.

Now it is split. Pripet Maior, the oldest covenant, a nest of ancient Bjornaer sinking into their heart-beasts, guards its marsh against settlers by raid and haunting; Thousand Caves in the Urals lives among pagan tribes, finds heart-beasts in mundanes, and seeks with the Volkhvy a way to temper auras and bring the god Hermes back. At the meeting of 1214 the quarrel broke into the open, and in 1217 Pripet Maior raided Thousand Caves without declaring Wizard's War. The magi have not yet been brought to judgement.

The meeting. The Tribunal meets every seven years at Three Lakes, which Pripet Maior ceded the privilege to more than forty years ago; the book dates meetings to 1214 and 1221 but gives no season, and summer is taken here. The Grand Tribunal of 1228 looms over it: the Rhine will use any scandal to press its claim to Poland.

Officers. The chief Quaesitor, Andrei Soitkchin of Three Lakes, chairs the meeting; Pavel Chedyav is his junior. The book names no Praeco: by the rule it is the eldest magus, Miya Cossuri of Pripet Maior, at a hundred and fifty-three, who seldom leaves her reed palace.

cases.title: The raid on Thousand Caves
cases.charge: An undeclared assault on a covenant of the Tribunal in the spring of 1217, meant to wreck its laboratories and kill its magi, with neither Wizard's War nor Wizard's March. Pripet Maior has ignored every summons; Casimi, who led it, is all but ungovernable, and too many magi have old ties to Pripet for punishment to be easy.
cases.evidence: The delegation's report; Thousand Caves' magi and animals; Otto Rattstein, who fought Casimi but will not lay charges before Crintera.

cases.title: Meddling with mundanes at Thousand Caves
cases.brought_by: Pripet Maior, with magi who were outraged in 1214
cases.charge: Thousand Caves leads a confederation of pagan tribes, teaches them a revived cult of Hermes and wakes heart-beasts in mundanes; the charge is interfering with the mundanes and endangering the Order. It is hard to prove harm, as the tribes are pagans hundreds of miles from any Christian authority.
cases.evidence: The delegation found Thousand Caves in breach of the Code in 1215-1216.

cases.title: Lelya Danichev's motion on the Volkhvy
cases.charge: That the Tribunal condemn the Order's treatment of the Volkhvy. Lelya also means to force Pripet Maior to a formal apology for the raid, and has practised certamen for three years to do it.

rulings.title: The settlement of new covenants
rulings.says: The Tribunal's council has formal authority over the settlement of every new covenant in the Slavic lands. Pushed through after the fall of Grand Silesia, when the Rhine's first attempt to move the border was only narrowly defeated at Grand Tribunal; it has been used several times since to eject trespassing bands of foreign magi, and some now say it has slowed the Tribunal's growth.

rulings.title: The Royal Embargo
rulings.says: No member of the Tribunal may reveal himself to any member of the Russian royal house. Made after the death of Mstislav the Great, when every alliance with a prince had ended in disaster; Yury Beslav of Three Lakes shaped it. Later extended to the Polish royal house. Leczyca and Pavel Chedyav resent it.

rulings.title: Leczyca's fine
rulings.says: Leczyca was found guilty of serious breaches of the Royal Embargo for giving Silesian nobles magically gained word of German raids, and paid a heavy fine in vis. The book dates it about thirty years before 1220.

diary.title: Michael of Amastris's expedition
diary.details: With Princess Olga driving off the Volkhvy, a Byzantine expedition under Michael of Amastris tries to found a covenant in the Drevlianian lands. Two magi are lost in Arcadia, one is killed by Volkhvy and one stoned in Kiev.

diary.title: Michael withdraws
diary.details: Sviatoslav, a pagan who cares only for war, lets Olga's policy lapse; the Volkhvy return in force and Michael flees to Constantinople before they strike.

diary.title: Rodnya founded
diary.details: The Theban Tribunal founds Rodnya on the Dnieper, about eighty miles south of Kiev.

diary.title: Grand Silesia and Pripet Maior founded
diary.details: The Rhine founds Grand Silesia between the Oder and the Warta, heavily backed by Crintera; Transylvania founds Pripet Maior in the Pripet marshes (the book's sidebar says 994).

diary.title: Patrick of Dunderry refuses
diary.details: Ordered by Thebes to join a strike on a Carpathian covenant, the quaesitor Patrick of Dunderry refuses and denounces the order as diabolical madness; Rodnya backs him, and the three covenants begin a quiet reconciliation.

diary.title: The New Slavonic Tribunal
diary.details: The three covenants shed their sponsors and declare themselves a Tribunal; the Grand Tribunal after the Schism War ratifies it.

diary.title: Rodnya abandoned
diary.details: Attacked by Thebans and Transylvanians alike, Rodnya is abandoned; Patrick leads its magi north. Grand Silesia is damaged and its refugees flee to Pripet Maior.

diary.title: Three Lakes founded
diary.details: Between lakes Onega, Beloe and Ilmen, equidistant from Novgorod, Beloozero and Ladoga.

diary.title: Grand Silesia destroyed
diary.details: Resettled in 1013, Grand Silesia is destroyed by anti-pagan knights when Casimir the Restorer returns to power; the Rhine makes its first attempt on the border.

diary.title: Leczyca founded
diary.details: Once Casimir has driven the Czechs from Silesia, Grand Silesia's survivors found Leczyca between the Vistula and the Warta; many stay at Pripet Maior, the root of its bond with House Bjornaer.

diary.title: The Novgorod Tribunal
diary.details: The Tribunal drops 'New' from its name and takes Novgorod's.

diary.title: Vseslav in Kiev
diary.details: Vseslav of Polotsk, a prince and a Volkhv, takes Kiev; the Tribunal, as in 1054, chooses to do nothing, and he is soon driven out. He dies in 1101, having written his dangerous lore in six great tomes of black serpent skin.

diary.title: The Royal Embargo
diary.details: After the death of Mstislav the Great the Tribunal forbids its members to reveal themselves to the Russian royal house.

diary.title: Roslav Lavickovich Primus
diary.details: Roslav of Pripet Maior is summoned to Crintera to become Primus of House Bjornaer, which he is for almost thirty years.

diary.title: Thousand Caves chartered
diary.details: On the urging of Malincka Capcek, the Tribunal grants a charter for a covenant in a gorge of the western Urals; Nastassia Baramov passes her Gauntlet at Three Lakes the day before.

diary.title: Leczyca fined
diary.details: Leczyca pays a heavy vis fine for aiding Silesian nobles against German raids.

diary.title: Pripet Maior's bicentenary
diary.details: The oldest covenant of the Tribunal marks two hundred years.

diary.title: Yannes Kolski's great Twilight
diary.details: The Criamon Yannes Kolski of Leczyca spends at least two weeks in Twilight, prophesying; his words, the Yannes Discourse, are kept at Leczyca. He never works magic again.

diary.title: Three Lakes' bicentenary
diary.details: A special council finds that no apprentice has passed a Gauntlet at Three Lakes in thirty-five years; four apprentices are taken in the five years after.

diary.title: The meeting dismissed
diary.details: Thousand Caves and Pripet Maior trade accusations; Malincka speaks for hours on how the Volkhvy temper auras. The Quaesitores confer in private, then dismiss the meeting, announcing a delegation to both covenants. They are also asked whether Yannes Kolski has passed into Final Twilight.

diary.title: The delegation
diary.details: A quaesitorial delegation backed by magi of every covenant visits Pripet Maior and Thousand Caves over 1215 and 1216, and finds both in breach of the Code.

diary.title: Yannes vanishes
diary.details: After a disruptive visit to Thousand Caves, Yannes Kolski is lost near Vladimir-in-Suzdalia while its magi escort him back.

diary.title: The raid on Thousand Caves
diary.details: Pripet Maior strikes Thousand Caves without declaring Wizard's War. It fails: the local animals stay loyal, two attackers fall into Twilight, and Otto Rattstein drives off Casimi Ljech as he is about to kill Nastassia Baramov.

diary.title: Zashya at Crintera
diary.details: Zashya Miyovna complains of Pripet Maior to the elders at Crintera, who summon Pripet to judgement but promise nothing to make it come.

tribunals.secrets:
Malincka Capcek hid her real purpose when she asked for Thousand Caves' charter in 1185: not a wilderness covenant but a way to blend Volkhv ritual with Hermetic magic, temper an aura with mundane worship and a faerie god, and make Hermes that god.

Zashya Miyovna of Three Lakes, daughter of the Praeco, bore a child to a prince of the House of Rurik before the Royal Embargo; her granddaughter is Nastassia Baramov of Thousand Caves.

neighbours.name: The Russian Principalities
neighbours.summary: The lands of the House of Rurik: Novgorod, Suzdalia, Ryazan, Smolensk, Polotsk, Chernigov, Kiev, Pereyaslavl, Pinsk-Turov, Volinia and Galicia, each ruled by its prince and his boyars and druzhina, at war with one another as often as not. Forest in the north, the open steppe in the south; rivers are the roads, timber, furs, wax, honey and slaves the trade. Pagan villages linger in the forests and the Volkhvy with them.

neighbours.name: The Lands of Lord Novgorod the Great
neighbours.summary: The vast northern lands of the city on the Volkhov, from Lake Ilmen to the White Sea: forest, lakes and fur-trapping country, with Ladoga and Beloozero its other towns.

neighbours.name: The Great Pripet Marsh
neighbours.summary:
Two hundred miles by a hundred and fifty of reed, channel, bog and stilt-village between Turov and Pinsk, rich in bog iron, fish and fowl, with salt basins beginning to be mined at its edge. Settlers are being brought in to drain and work it, and Pripet Maior answers them with raids and hauntings.

The marsh's heart is a wilderness few enter; Stolitzya the Swimmer is said to brood there.

neighbours.name: The Western Urals
neighbours.summary: Endless forest rising to the mountains in the east, above the headwaters of the Kama. Three Lakes' explorers reached it in the 1150s; its Slavic tribes are quietly pagan and live with little iron.

neighbours.name: The Kingdom of Poland
neighbours.summary: The lands of the Piast dukes, divided since 1138 into duchies: Krakow and Sandomierz under the Grand Duke Leszek the White, Silesia, Greater Poland, Mazovia and Kujavia, and Pomerania on the sea. German settlers pour into Silesia, the Prussians raid from the north, and the Rhine Tribunal covets the land, which it calls vacant.

neighbours.name: The Baltic Coast
neighbours.summary: The pagan peoples' shore: Prussians, Lithuanians, Samogithians, Curs, Semgallians, Livonians, Letts and Estonians, with the crusading orders, the Bishop of Riga and the Danes pressing in. Where the old gods are still the law, the Volkhvy are priests of whole peoples.

neighbours.name: The Southern Steppe
neighbours.summary: The open grassland south of Kiev and Pereyaslavl, the Cumans' range for a century, where nomads have come and gone for millennia. Rodnya stood at its edge.

neighbours.name: The Valley of Three Lakes
neighbours.summary: A fertile lowland valley ringed by dense woods at the centre of the triangle of lakes Onega, Beloe and Ilmen, much of its floor a wide, placid lake; its walls and some of the floor are cleared for pasture. The covenant's stockade climbs from the Trade Yard to the High House and the stone Keep in a pass of the valley wall.

neighbours.name: The Valley of a Thousand Caves
neighbours.summary:
A long, twisting gorge running down from the western face of the Urals above the Kama's headwaters, its cliffs pocked with hundreds of dry, roomy caves joined by ledges. At its mouth rears the Earth Crown, the covenant's watchpost; below it the Great Cavern, as large as a cathedral, is the only fortified part. The valley floor is farmed. Georgi Yurivich found and named it more than forty years ago.

A Slavic faerie aura: to most people and magic no different from any Faerie aura, but the Volkhvy draw twice its strength in their rites there, and pagans with Pagan Belief can work domestic magic in it. The Volkhvy keep such auras Slavic; without them they turn neutral.

neighbours.name: Pripet Maior's Island
neighbours.summary: A middling island twenty miles inside the southern edge of the marsh, reached by one narrow path from the south and then a deep channel crossed by an enchanted causeway, which the Aegis raises for covenfolk and invited guests (and which sticks up or down when the Aegis is late). Its reed palaces, living tree houses and flower arbours were once a baroque marvel; now they rot, and quicksand lies among them.

neighbours.name: Leczyca's Ridge
neighbours.summary: A ridge in gentle hill country between the Vistula and the Warta, about fifty miles east of Sieradz. The east and west approaches are rough, the south tedious; an easy track climbs from the north, from Leczyca town.

neighbours.name: Rodnya
neighbours.summary: The Theban covenant founded near the town of Rodnya on the Dnieper, eighty miles south of Kiev, in 992; Patrick of Dunderry's home, abandoned in 1009 under Theban and Transylvanian attack.

neighbours.name: Grand Silesia
neighbours.summary: The Rhine's covenant of 993, in a secluded valley of the hills between the Oder and the Warta, halfway between Poznan and Wroclaw; damaged in 1009, resettled in 1013 and destroyed by anti-pagan knights in 1039.

neighbours.name: Lake Strukhalis
neighbours.summary: The Polish lake where belief in Strukis the Great Pike, king of fish and lord of the water faeries, is strongest. His palace lies beneath it; whoever enters stands a good chance of being seized as his slave.

neighbours.name: The Tatra Mountains
neighbours.summary: The north-western Carpathians on Poland's southern border, where most of the Slavic monsters lair: dragons, ogres and giants (dziwozony), and lesser horrors that raid the borderland.

neighbours.name: Wawel Hill
neighbours.summary: Krakow's citadel hill, where the hero Krakus slew a marauding dragon by an alchemical trick he could not manage by arms; the city grew on the site. The cave beneath is still shown.

neighbours.name: Slavic Arcadia
neighbours.summary:
The part of Arcadia ruled by the faerie powers the Slavs call gods: firmer and more logical than the west's, a land of fairy tale where kindness to an overladen tree is rewarded and giants come in threes. The World Tree holds it together: Slavic Heaven in its branches, Slavic Earth (thirty princedoms, half of the Gold Court and half of the White) about its trunk, and Slavic Hell among its roots, where the Nameless God of Demons is bound and the Fates watch, and where the dead live in the autumn garden of Slavic Elysium with the Isle of Boyan, home of the Volkhvy's dead.

Visitors are drawn at once into its stories; those who play them too well stay happily ever after. Every foray should cost something. Since 1206 Mongol spirits, wingless thunder wyrms, have raided it in the Onslaught, laying three princedoms waste.

levels.name: Slavic Earth
levels.notes: An idealized Russia of princedoms and cities about the World Tree's mountain; its borders with the 'German' faeries are the way into western Arcadia.

levels.name: Slavic Heaven
levels.notes: The gods' world in the Tree's branches, of blinding Summer; only the strongest Volkhvy go, and few return.

levels.name: Slavic Hell and Elysium
levels.notes: Dim courts of winter and toil, the dark gods' realm where the Fates keep the Nameless, and the gentle Elysium of the pagan dead with the Isle of Boyan.

neighbours.name: Yury II Vsevolodovich, Grand Prince of Vladimir
neighbours.summary: Grand Prince of Suzdalia since 1218, after the war among Vsevolod III's sons that his brother Konstantin won in 1216. The strongest prince of the north; his brother Yaroslav will be called to rule Novgorod in 1221. If history holds he dies against the Mongols in 1238, caught on open ground before his brothers can join him.

neighbours.name: Mstislav the Daring, Prince of Galicia
neighbours.summary: Mstislav Mstislavich, who left Novgorod in 1219 and has ruled Galicia since, a famous warrior and son-in-law of the Cuman Khan Kotian. It is he who will raise the princes against the Mongols in 1223 and lead them to the Kalka.

neighbours.name: Mstislav Romanovich, Prince of Kiev
neighbours.summary: Of the Rostislavichi, who hold Kiev from 1212 to 1235. If history holds he makes the last stand at the Kalka in 1223 and is smothered under a carpet by the Mongols, as befits royalty, for the murder of their envoys.

neighbours.name: Mstislav Svyatoslavich, Prince of Chernigov
neighbours.summary: Head of the Olgavichi, whose two lines rule Chernigov and Novgorod-Seversk; he too dies at the Kalka, if history holds.

neighbours.name: Daniil Romanovich, Prince of Volinia
neighbours.summary: The young son of Roman of Galicia, killed at Zawichost in 1205, and of his widow Anna; rising fast in Volinia. If history holds he wins Kiev in 1240 just before the Mongols destroy it, and submits to them in 1241.

neighbours.name: Ingvar Igorevich, Prince of Ryazan
neighbours.summary: Prince of Ryazan and Murom on the steppe's edge, the first land the Mongols will burn in 1237. (The book names no one for 1220; history's ruler is taken.)

neighbours.name: Mstislav Davydovich, Prince of Smolensk
neighbours.summary: Of the Rostislavichi, ruling the trading city of Smolensk on the upper Dnieper. (The book names no one for 1220; history's ruler is taken.)

neighbours.name: Vsevolod Mstislavich, Prince of Novgorod
neighbours.summary: Son of the Prince of Kiev, called by Novgorod after Mstislav the Daring left in 1219. Novgorod's princes rule at the Veche's pleasure; the book says those after Mstislav failed, and in 1221 the city expels them and calls Yaroslav, Yury's brother, beginning a war with Chernigov that lasts until 1230. (The book names no one for 1220; history's ruler is taken.)

neighbours.name: Mikhail of Turov
neighbours.summary: A boyar of Pinsk-Turov who has hunted the 'marsh monsters' in force, talks of summoning harpoonists from distant Norway, and means to dig canals to the Pripet and drain the marsh for pasture, dealing firmly with any opposition. He thinks he faces wild beasts or faeries, not magi.
neighbours.secrets: The Church may be brought in if he finds solid proof of supernatural meddling, and Pripet Maior is no secret in the district.

neighbours.name: Valdemar II of Denmark
neighbours.summary: The Victorious, King of Denmark, who has conquered northern Estonia since 1219 and holds Reval; the Estonians will rise against the Danes in 1223.

neighbours.name: Leszek the White, Grand Duke of Krakow
neighbours.summary: Duke of Sandomierz, who seized Krakow and the senior throne in 1202 and invaded Volinia from 1214 to 1218. He will be killed in 1227.

neighbours.name: Henry the Bearded, Duke of Silesia
neighbours.summary: Duke of Silesia since 1201, who has brought German settlers into his lands since 1205; he dies in 1238. His son Henry the Pious will fall at Legnica.

neighbours.name: Conrad of Mazovia
neighbours.summary: Duke of Mazovia and Kujavia, harried by the Prussians, who early in the 1220s will invite the Teutonic Knights to Chelmno to fight them.

neighbours.name: Wladislaw Spindleshanks, Duke of Greater Poland
neighbours.summary: Duke of Greater Poland, the land about Gniezno and Poznan.

neighbours.name: Swietopelk of Pomerania
neighbours.summary: Prince of eastern Pomerania from 1220, after Mestwin I (whom the Rhine pack keeps as prince in its year); he will break with the Polish dukes.

neighbours.name: The Count of Leczyca
neighbours.summary: The lord of the town below the covenant, and Stanis Chechenko's patron. The book does not name him.

neighbours.name: Sancta Sophia of Kiev
neighbours.summary: The seat of the Metropolitan of Kiev, head of the Russian Church, Matfey (1209-1224), a Greek appointed from Constantinople. The Church is the princes' mediator and the Volkhvy's enemy; its white clergy marry, its black clergy are monks, and the Archbishop of Novgorod is second to the Metropolitan. Sees: Belgorod, Chernigov, Galich, Peremyshl, Pereyaslavl, Polotsk, Rostov, Ryazan, Smolensk, Suzdal, Turov, Vladimir-in-Suzdalia, Vladimir-in-Volinia and Tmutorokan. There is no inquisition. Saints have taken the old gods' places: Elijah Perun's, Mary Mati-Syra-Zemlya's, Paraskeva Mokosh's, Vlas Volos's.

neighbours.name: Sancta Sophia of Novgorod
neighbours.summary: The Archbishop's cathedral in the Kremlin of Novgorod, whose lord is a power in the city's government. The book does not name him.

neighbours.name: The Monastery of the Caves
neighbours.summary: The great monastery dug into the bluffs of the Dnieper at Kiev, the heart of Russian monasticism.

neighbours.name: Gniezno Cathedral
neighbours.summary: The seat of the Polish Church in the old capital. Archbishop Henry Kietlicz (1199-1219), who fought for the Church's freedom from the dukes, has just died; the book does not name his successor. (The book names no one for 1220; history's ruler is taken.)
neighbours.ruler: Wincenty of Niałek, Archbishop of Gniezno

neighbours.name: Riga Cathedral
neighbours.summary: Albert, Bishop of Riga since 1200, founder of the Brotherhood of the Knights of the Sword, who are conquering Livonia in his name.

neighbours.name: Novgorod
neighbours.summary: Lord Novgorod the Great on the Volkhov, a trading republic: its Veche, the assembly of free men, elects the Posadnik (mayor) and Tysiatsky, and calls and dismisses princes; the boyars' council, the Sovet Gospod, guides it. Five districts, the Hanse's Peterhof, the cathedral of Sancta Sophia. Sadko the merchant is its folk hero. Three Lakes' trade rivals are here.

neighbours.name: Ladoga
neighbours.summary: Novgorod's northern town on the Volkhov near Lake Ladoga, where Three Lakes buys its luxuries.

neighbours.name: Beloozero
neighbours.summary: The town on Lake Beloe, one of the three civilized places Three Lakes sits between.

neighbours.name: Kiev
neighbours.summary: Mother of Russian cities, much fought over and past its greatness, with the Metropolitan's court and the Monastery of the Caves. If history holds it is stormed by the Mongols on 6 December 1240 and left a waste.

neighbours.name: Vladimir-in-Suzdalia
neighbours.summary: The Grand Prince's capital; Yannes Kolski vanished near it in 1216. The Mongols will burn it in 1238.

neighbours.name: Smolensk
neighbours.summary: The Rostislavichi's trading city on the upper Dnieper.

neighbours.name: Chernigov
neighbours.summary: The Olgavichi's seat, which the Mongols will crush in 1240.

neighbours.name: Polotsk
neighbours.summary: Vseslav the Sorcerer's city, raided by Lithuanians.

neighbours.name: Galich
neighbours.summary: The capital of Galicia under the Carpathians.

neighbours.name: Turov
neighbours.summary: The town at the marsh's edge, seat of Mikhail of Turov.

neighbours.name: Krakow
neighbours.summary: The Grand Duke's city under Wawel Hill, where Krakus slew the dragon.

neighbours.name: Wroclaw
neighbours.summary: Silesia's capital, filling with German settlers.

neighbours.name: Gniezno
neighbours.summary: Poland's old capital and the seat of its archbishop.

neighbours.name: Leczyca
neighbours.summary: The town north of the covenant's ridge, whose name it took.

neighbours.name: Sieradz
neighbours.summary: A town about fifty miles west of the covenant.

neighbours.name: Riga
neighbours.summary: The crusaders' city at the mouth of the Dvina, seat of the Bishop and the Knights of the Sword.

neighbours.name: Great Bulgar
neighbours.summary: The Muslim city of the Volga Bulgars, a great market for the east; home of Yakim ibn Rassur and the scholar Haroun Hashemi. The Mongols will raze it in 1237.

neighbours.name: The Teutonic Knights
neighbours.summary: The German crusading order, its headquarters at Montfort near Acre; Conrad of Mazovia will soon invite it to fight the Prussians, and its Prussian crusade begins in 1230. The military orders carry a wrathful Divine aura (Pax Dei).

neighbours.name: The Knights of the Sword
neighbours.summary: The Brotherhood of the Sword, founded by Bishop Albert of Riga, conquering Livonia; they took Fellin in 1211. Any Baltic saga must reckon with them.

details.wants: The Baltic pagans converted or conquered

neighbours.name: The Baltic Pagans
neighbours.summary: The Prussians, Lithuanians, Samogithians, Curs, Selonians, Semgallians, Livonians, Letts and Estonians, who keep the old gods with their priests (the Lithuanians' Vorschatyen, the Prussians' Waidelots) and their house snakes, the zaltys. The Lithuanians raid Polotsk; the Estonians will rise in 1223; a papal legate, William of Modena, comes in 1225.

neighbours.name: The Cumans
neighbours.summary: The nomads of the southern steppe, a branch of the Kipchaks; Batiba of Three Lakes is one. Khan Kotian is Mstislav the Daring's father-in-law. If history holds the Mongols break them in 1223, and in 1239 Kotian leads forty thousand into Hungary.

neighbours.name: The Volkhvy
neighbours.summary:
The Slavs' pagan priest-wizards (Znachor in Poland, Waidelots in Prussia, Vorschatyen in Lithuania), who held the Order out until the princes turned Christian, and still keep the rites in pagan villages, where faeries greet them as cousins. They keep their villages' auras Slavic, and their Pagan Conviction is their Magic Resistance. The Tribunal officially ignores them; Thousand Caves admits them.

Their gods are great faerie lords of Slavic Arcadia, beyond statistics: Svarog of fire and the sky and his sons Svarozhich, Dazhdbog and Khors; Perun of thunder and war; Mati-Syra-Zemlya the earth; Ersvorsh of weather and Stribog of the winds; Volos of poetry, oracles and trade; Mokosh, Kupala and Beilbog of healing and women; the three Zorya; Baba Yaga of death; the dark Chernobog, Kolyada and the Nameless God of Demons, whose priests are Koldun; and the Baltic Dievs, Saule, Mehnesis, Zemlja and the rest.

details.rules: Each serves a principal god and a pagan community, and sings his magic; most are illiterate, their lore oral

neighbours.name: The Vedun
neighbours.summary: The Slavs' cunning folk, and every pagan household: in a Slavic faerie aura, ordinary believers can charm a loom to weave through the night, bless a field or ensure a safe birth by domestic magic.

neighbours.name: The Beslavichi
neighbours.summary: The prosperous trading family the north takes Three Lakes for, with reindeer sleds and agents across north Russia and the Baltic; its patriarch and his son are its magi.

neighbours.name: The Cult of Hermes
neighbours.summary: The faith Thousand Caves has preached to its tribes for thirty years, with new festivals, rites and idols of Hermes in the Great Cavern's sanctum; Nastassia leads its rites, and the girl Stenya Vassanovna says Lord Hermes speaks to her.

neighbours.name: The German Merchants of the Peterhof
neighbours.summary: The German traders' court at Novgorod, the Baltic trade's eastern end.

neighbours.name: The Mongol Conquest
neighbours.summary:
As 1220 opens Genghis Khan is camped before Bukhara with a great part of his horde. He has come for the Khwarazm-shah, whose governor at Otrar killed his merchants and who shamed and killed his envoys, and the shah's empire from the Jaxartes to the Gulf is about to fall. The cities the Mongols sack and leave empty may take Infernal auras of wrath, which draw lesser demons, dark faeries, ghuls and evil jinn in the horde's wake, and the unburied dead wander.

If history holds, the Mongols take Persia, Georgia, Armenia, northern Iraq and Asia Minor in the decades after, sack Baghdad in 1258, and are stopped only by Egypt's Mamluks in Syria in 1260. The Levant's magi know almost nothing of them yet.

In Russia and Poland, if history holds, they come twice: a reconnaissance that breaks the princes on the Kalka in 1223, and from 1237 a conquest that burns Ryazan, Vladimir, Chernigov and Kiev, ravages Poland and Hungary, and lays the Mongol yoke on Russia for two centuries. Their spirits run ahead of them: since 1206 wingless thunder wyrms have raided Slavic Arcadia in the Onslaught, and their spies and shamans work among the princes long before the horde returns.

stages.title: Bukhara falls
stages.ignored: The town falls within a fortnight; its defenders are killed, its people enslaved or driven off, and fire leaves it in ruins under an Infernal aura of 3, save round the Kalyan minaret.

stages.title: Samarkand and the Jaxartes towns
stages.ignored: The horde, swelled by Turkish recruits, destroys the oasis towns along the Jaxartes as far as Khojend and takes Samarkand.

stages.title: Gurganj and the shah
stages.ignored: Gurganj falls and its great dykes are broken; the shah is hunted across Khurasan to die on the Caspian shore; Baylaqan in the west is razed.

stages.title: Into Persia
stages.ignored: Balkh, Merv, Nishapur and Herat are sacked, the shah's son is driven over the Indus, and Jebe and Subadei ride north into Russia.

stages.title: The Kalka
stages.clues: Refugee Cumans beg the Russian princes for help; Mongol envoys come with gifts.
stages.ignored: Subadei, having bought off and then destroyed the Cumans, draws the princes' host into a nine-day pursuit and routes it on the Kalka: nine princes die, the Prince of Kiev smothered under a carpet for the murdered envoys. Then the Mongols ride home past the Volga Bulgars, and the Russians forget them.

stages.title: The return
stages.clues: Mongol spies along the steppe; the princes at war over Kiev.
stages.ignored: Great Bulgar is razed; in December the horde enters Ryazan, then burns Vladimir and kills the Grand Prince. Northern Russia submits in four months; Novgorod is spared by the thaw.

stages.title: Kiev falls
stages.ignored: Chernigov and Pereyaslavl are crushed, and on 6 December Kiev is stormed and left a field of bones.

stages.title: Legnica and the Sajo
stages.ignored: Two toumens sack Sandomierz and Krakow and destroy Henry the Pious's army at Legnica; a day later Batu and Subadei annihilate the Hungarian host on the Sajo.

stages.title: The horde turns back
stages.ignored: Word of Ogedei's death recalls Subadei; Batu withdraws to the Volga steppe, razing as he goes, and rules Russia from Sarai.

neighbours.name: The Trial of Pripet Maior
neighbours.summary: The raid of 1217 cannot go unpunished, yet Pripet Maior ignores every summons, Casimi Ljech is all but ungovernable, Crintera will not force the magi to come, and too many of the Tribunal's magi owe Pripet old loyalties. The meeting of 1221 must try it, and Thousand Caves too, with the Grand Tribunal of 1228 and the Rhine watching for a scandal.

stages.title: The meeting of 1221
stages.clues: Magi canvass Three Lakes; Lelya Danichev practises certamen; Pripet's magi may or may not come.
stages.ignored: The Tribunal fails to act, Pripet Maior grows bolder, and House Bjornaer's quarrel goes to the Gathering.
stages.stopped: Pripet Maior is fined, its magi bound to the peace, or a Wizard's March is declared on Casimi.
stages.turned: A troupe that brings Pripet Maior to Three Lakes, or Casimi to heel, sways the verdict.

neighbours.name: Draining the Pripet
neighbours.summary: Mikhail of Turov has hunted the marsh's monsters, talked of Norwegian harpoonists, and now means to dig canals to the Pripet and drain the land for pasture, crushing anyone who objects. The army that digs will meet Pripet Maior's raids and hauntings, and if he finds proof of magic he may call the Church. Crintera will claim Pripet's legacy if it falls.

stages.title: The diggers arrive
stages.clues: Surveyors on the marsh's southern edge; levies gathered at Turov.
stages.ignored: Pripet Maior strikes the diggers; men die, and Mikhail sends for priests and harpoonists.

stages.title: War in the marsh
stages.clues: Stories of beasts that fight like men and men who turn into beasts.
stages.ignored: Pripet Maior is exposed or destroyed; the Order's presence in Russia is in danger.
stages.stopped: The draining is turned aside, by magic or by persuasion, without the Order being seen.

neighbours.name: Malincka's Great Work
neighbours.summary: Malincka is designing a spell of magnitude 11, a development of Read the Magic Sphere with something of Plumb the Magical Scent, at Touch, with a Mentem requisite, to let other magi see auras exactly and how minds move them. Her Lab Total is 69; even so she must experiment to finish within the year. With it she hopes to win the Tribunal at the meeting of 1221 and then devise a Hermetic Great Ritual. Whether aura-making can succeed is the troupe's to decide (p. 120).

stages.title: The spell, or not
stages.clues: Malincka's laboratory runs every season; experiments go spectacularly wrong.
stages.ignored: She comes to the meeting with the spell, or with a failure that hands her enemies a weapon.
stages.turned: A troupe that helps her shapes what the spell reveals, and what the Tribunal sees.

neighbours.name: The Return of Hermes
neighbours.summary: For thirty years Thousand Caves has preached Hermes to its tribes, hoping a great faerie will take up the god's part. Surges of magic and ecstatic dreams have begun, Basyl has visions of Hermes's coming, and the girl Stenya Vassanovna, Gifted, says Lord Hermes speaks to her and preaches him persuasively; even Rehamchi half believes her. The magi fear they will draw a demon instead.

stages.title: Something answers
stages.clues: Stenya's sermons grow stranger; the aura shifts.
stages.ignored: A power takes the name of Hermes: a faerie with its own agenda, a demon, or the Slavic gods' anger.
stages.turned: A troupe that learns what speaks to Stenya decides what kind of god comes.

neighbours.name: Where Is Yannes Kolski?
neighbours.summary: The Mad Magus of the East vanished near Vladimir-in-Suzdalia in 1216, still reciting his vision of the black serpent from the east. Is he dead, in Final Twilight, taken by faeries, or gone east to meet what he foresaw? The Yannes Discourse at Leczyca may say more than anyone has read in it.

stages.title: A sighting
stages.clues: A howling holy fool among the Cumans; a merchant repeats the serpent verses.
stages.ignored: The Discourse's warning goes unread until the Mongols come.

neighbours.name: Stolitzya the Swimmer
neighbours.summary: Pripet Maior's founder, lost forty years in her turtle heart-beast, may still brood in the marsh's heart, its queen. If the draining or a war reaches her, she will rise.

stages.title: The island that moves
stages.clues: Floating islands torn apart; boats shattered from beneath.
stages.ignored: Stolitzya wakes against whoever troubles the marsh, magi or mundanes.

neighbours.name: Zashya's Secret
neighbours.summary: Zashya Miyovna bore a daughter to a Rurikid prince, and her granddaughter is Nastassia Baramov. Revealed, it would shame Zashya before the Royal Embargo's makers, make Nastassia a prince's kin, and tell Miya Cossuri that the maga Pripet loathes is her great-granddaughter.

stages.title: The secret is out
stages.clues: Questions about Nastassia's parents; an old servant of the prince's house.
stages.ignored: The quarrel between Pripet and Thousand Caves becomes a family feud.

neighbours.name: Leczyca and the Rhine
neighbours.summary: Rhine interlopers raid Polish vis, Durenmar's agents work against Leczyca, and Leczyca's sympathy for the Polish nobles tempts it to intervene by magic against the Germans, as it did before its fine.

details.antagonist: Durenmar and the lesser Rhine covenants

stages.title: A battle with the Germans
stages.clues: A Silesian lord asks for help; a Rhine magus is seen near Wroclaw.
stages.ignored: Leczyca intervenes, breaks the Embargo again, and gives the Rhine its scandal.

neighbours.name: The Gathering of the Twelve Years
neighbours.summary: House Bjornaer's Gathering is due in 1227, and Pripet Maior and Thousand Caves have both put their cases at Crintera. The raid has raised the stakes; the Gathering is bound to be explosive.

stages.title: The Gathering
stages.ignored: The House judges between Pripet Maior and Thousand Caves, or splits over them.

neighbours.name: Durenmar's Motion
neighbours.summary: At every Grand Tribunal Durenmar moves that the Rhine's eastern border be reassessed. If the quarrel over Thousand Caves reaches the Grand Tribunal of 1228 as a scandal, the Rhine may at last take the 'vacant' Polish lands.

stages.title: The Grand Tribunal of 1228
stages.ignored: The motion is heard with the Tribunal's troubles before the whole Order.
stages.stopped: The Tribunal settles its quarrel first and the motion fails, as before.

characters.name: Andrei Soitkchin

description.biography:
Chief Quaesitor, an office of House Guernicus. Rheumatism and a leg weakened in Twilight. His Cloak of Silken Steel, made by Nicollo decades ago, is a formal robe of dark blue and grey silk that turns violence like supple mail: Protection 10, no Load. The book has him master every listed spell of InMe, InIm, PeIm, ReCo, ReIm, ReMe and ReVi, with enhanced truth, lie-detection and compulsion spells of his own, and defensive spells of invisibility, teleportation and mind domination.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 122 as printed; Twilight Points 16 / 3 = Warping 5; Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 4. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.
Virtues and Flaws: Quaesitor dropped (an office of House Guernicus, not a Virtue now; the office is noted); Magical Affinity as Affinity with Intellego; Strong-willed as Strong-Willed; Visual Eidetic Memory dropped (not in the catalog); Weak Parma Magica dropped (the catalog's Flawed Parma Magica is weak against one Form, not when unaware); Non-combatant as Noncombatant.
Abilities: Certamen 7 to Penetration; Disputatio 4 to Teaching; Hermes Lore 6 to Organization Lore: Order of Hermes; Hermetic Law 6 to Code of Hermes; Magic Affinity 4 to Intellego, 10 xp; Scribe Latin 5 to Artes Liberales; Scribe Cyrillic 4 to Artes Liberales.

characters.summary: Senior, chief Quaesitor of the Tribunal and chairman of Three Lakes' council, who sees that its magi keep its detailed charter and the Code. Patient, scrupulous, severe and famed for humourless impartiality. His first task is to discipline Pripet Maior for its raid, which is proving all but impossible. He specializes in truth, lie-detection and compulsion, and escapes trouble by invisibility, teleportation and mind domination.

characters.name: Pavel Chedyav

description.biography: The Dragon and the Bear: The Novgorod Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 100 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Senior, the junior Quaesitor and Andrei's evident successor, which pleases him. An ingenious magus and a fine laboratory worker, he sees the Thousand Caves debate as an intellectual puzzle. He came from Leczyca about fifty years ago, leans to Poland, wants the Polish realm reunited and the Tribunal moved out of Russia, and resents the Royal Embargo though he keeps it. He helped Nicollo make the Eye of Magic.

characters.name: Yury Beslav

params.circumstance: alone: magic works only with two or more people present

description.biography:
Balding, rheumatic and short-sighted. His Deleterious Circumstances, worsened from major to total in Twilight, is the Definitive Edition's Minor Flaw here, though his magic fails altogether when he is alone. His quarterstaff is enchanted to stony hardness (Damage +6), his fur robes to strength and resistance (Protection +5). The book has him master every listed spell of InCo, InIm, InMe, ReCo, ReIm and ReMe, and abhor flashy destructive magic.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 117 as printed; Twilight Points 20 / 3 = Warping 6; Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 4. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.
Virtues and Flaws: Well Traveled as Well-Traveled; Deep Sleeper dropped (not in the catalog).
Abilities: Brawling 3 to Brawl; Certamen 5 to Penetration; Disputatio 3 to Teaching; Hermes Lore 5 to Organization Lore: Order of Hermes; Hermetic Law 4 to Code of Hermes; Scribe Bulgar 3 to Artes Liberales; Scribe Latin 6 to Artes Liberales; Scribe Cyrillic 4 to Artes Liberales; Storytelling 4 to Living Language: Russian; Wagoneering 3 to Profession: Teamster.

characters.summary: Senior and the covenant's public face, patriarch of the Beslavichi: a traditional Jerbiton in district politics, trade and the patronage of artists, a part he has played so long it is no act. He shaped the Royal Embargo after finding that no friendship with a prince stays small. His magic works only in the company of two or more people, so he keeps grogs in his laboratory and scribes at his secret meetings. Apprentice: Mina Dankovna.

characters.name: Georgi Yurivich

description.biography: The Dragon and the Bear: The Novgorod Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 95 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Senior, Yury's son, apprentice and heir, with magic much like his father's. For thirty years he has run the trading journeys, often in Ladoga and Novgorod or on the northern trails meeting agents and informants. He found and named the Valley of a Thousand Caves more than forty years ago and led Malincka there in 1182; she is his friend, and her work now troubles him. Having aged too little for the mundanes who know him, he wears an enhanced Disguise of the New Visage and turns awkward questions aside with Mentem.

characters.name: Batiba an Khatiba
characters.summary: Senior, the one member who is not a Hermetic magus: a Cuman shaman who worships his ancestors and the spirits of earth and sky, brought from the steppe by Georgi about fifty years ago and joined to the Order as a hedge wizard. The Quaesitores made him their authority on pagan matters and a pillar of the delegation. He is enthusiastic for Thousand Caves, which is nearer the society he knows than the Order is, and longs to spread word of it among Ex Miscellanea; so far he has been restrained, just.

characters.name: Zashya Miyovna

description.biography:
Swan heart-beast, not battle-worthy, its shape hidden. Claustrophobic; short of breath. Her Cloak of Silken Feathers, Nicollo's gift, is snow-white silk stitched with tiny diamonds: Protection 4, and at a word it becomes a feather mantle that merges with her swan's plumage. The book has her extremely powerful in CrAu, CrAn, MuAu and MuAn, with Aquam and Corpus requisites, knowing few formulaics outside them; she can work enhanced versions of most combat CrAu spells.

On the delegation she tried to reconcile her House, and was preached at by Thousand Caves and threatened by Pripet Maior, above all by Miya Cossuri, her mother and parens. Her complaint at Crintera in 1218 came to nothing. She specializes in weather and animals. Apprentice: Ratibor Peslav.

One of the age's great travellers: she went with Sadko the merchant in the 1160s and 1170s, later with Georgi into the east, from Sweden to Constantinople. Every year she makes a full circuit of the covenants without the portal, to keep it hidden, coming home by the Leap of Homecoming. Apolitical, proud of the Redcaps. She says she saw Stolitzya about fifteen years ago. Apprentice: Dankya Yostovna.

A famous teacher, generous on Faerie Lore and Etiquette, her summae and questions the library's pride, but secretive about her spells. Rumour says she has solved faerie time, can wipe away fatigue, and siphons Might from friendly faeries. She is dismissive of Thousand Caves. Apprentice: Kassim ibn Fadal.

He believes animals have legends that may hold the wisdom of the world before man, has sought beast lords in Arcadia and griffins, chimeras, pegasi and unicorns in the wild, and records all he finds. He would not join the delegation, though he went with Zashya to Crintera.

Untested in violence or politics, he is beginning to feel he must speak: drawn to Thousand Caves' experiment, yet in sympathy with the vis-hungry western Tribunals. He made Andrei's cloak and Zashya's.

invented_spells.name: Charge the Magical Circle
invented_spells.description: A Ritual blending Hermetic method with Volkhv dance and sung invocations to Slavic gods, which raises a small circular magic aura where none was: +1 for one extra pawn of vis beyond the Ritual's, +2 for three, +3 for six, and so on up the pyramid (none extra gives a worthless +0). Cast always with six botch dice; cast where an aura exists it fails, with as many more botch dice as the aura's strength, and other things nearby can twist it (Herbam vis at its edge once raised a +10 aura and opened a gate to the Spirit Lands). Malincka thinks it useless without mundanes to steady it. The book's level stands, and leaves open whether aura-making can truly work (p. 120).

invented_spells.name: Read the Magic Sphere
invented_spells.description: Her newest aura spell, eight years old: she sees any aura, chiefly by sight, to the limit of her view, and may walk its bounds. She knows its realm at once; a Perception roll tells its strength up to 7 (9+), the way to its centre (12+) and its age (15+). With Magic Sensitivity all that comes freely, with +5 to Sensitivity, and Per + Sensitivity asks whether it is stable, waning or growing (12+), its source and whether another aura was there before (15+), how long ago and of what kind (18+), and its strength (21+). The book's level stands.

invented_spells.name: Plumb the Magical Scent
invented_spells.description: Her first study of how a Great Ritual touches its worshippers' minds: tells whether a human mind is under magic's influence, and a Per + Magic Sensitivity stress roll of 9+ gives details. Useful but imprecise, and its fleeting duration makes it clumsy. The book's level stands.

invented_spells.name: Air of Friendly Magic
invented_spells.description: A Ritual, again of blended method, that turns a small area of Faerie aura of 6 or less into a Magic aura of the same strength. It needs six mundane assistants making Hermetic gestures and Volkhv chants, whose part steadies it for reasons she does not yet know. Cast with three extra botch dice; spells cast in the changed aura have two, and the aura stays faerie-tainted, so spells show fay traits and botches bring bizarre faerie manifestations. The book's level stands; whether aura-making can truly work the book leaves open (p. 120).

description.biography:
Higher Purpose: to unite the Order of Hermes and mundanes. Driven: to invent a blended theory of Volkhv and Hermetic magic. Liver-spotted, stiff in the hips. Her Twilights gave her more Vim and an insight into Volkhv magic.

characters.summary: The covenant's ideological leader, a Hungarian Bonisagus. Thirty-five years ago, in a Twilight while watching a Great Ritual, she saw why four centuries of Hermetic attempts on auras failed: the power needs magical ritual, a fount of faerie power and, she believes, mundane people to channel it. Her aims: a Hermetic Great Ritual that tempers auras; an aura that gives magi what a Slavic aura gives Volkhvy, and at last one aura for both; Volkhv Disciplines broadened like Arts with quick formulaic forms; and the force behind domestic magic, for her own covenfolk. Her aura-making and aura-reading spells are her own. Compassionate, impetuous, proud of her House.

A battle-worthy beast gains +5 Attack and Damage and +15 Soak, any other +3, +3 and +10, and neither feels wounds or fatigue until it falls. Spell focus a part of such an animal (+2). The book's level stands.

invented_spells.name: Echo of the Firebird
invented_spells.description: Nastassia's newest heart-beast spell: her eagle grows toward an ideal Firebird, Size +1, Attack +5, Damage +8 and Soak +15, untroubled by wounds or fatigue until it drops; feathers, talons and beak gleam ruddy gold and trail wisps of flame in flight, and it radiates heat, touching it like touching a torch. Not cumulative with Form of the Avenging Beast. The book's level stands.

characters.summary: 'The Firebird', Malincka's second, with the force of character her leader lacks: a Bjornaer with an eagle heart-beast and a rare bent for Ignem, obsessed since childhood with the Firebird, whose lore she has hunted far and toward whose form her own spells reshape her eagle. She shocked Pripet Maior at her Gauntlet at Three Lakes, the day before Thousand Caves was chartered, by showing a heart-beast limned in flame. The most serious of the magi in the worship of Hermes and a devotee of Khors, leader of the search for heart-beasts among the tribes. Yakim is her lover. Casimi Ljech nearly killed her in 1217. She does not know who her grandmother is.

characters.name: Rehamchi Danichev

description.biography:
A Volkhv, priest of Khors, with Pagan Conviction 6. His Fourth Edition Disciplines are kept here as the book prints them, not converted: Spirit Touch 6, Healing 7, Shapeshift 6, Weatherworking 9, Animal Magic 8, Remove Curse 10, Prophecy 7, Sun Magic 11 and Earth Magic 6; Khors gives him +5 Sun Magic, +3 Spirit Touch, +3 to the Great Ritual and +3 to shift into a golden horse, and -5 Earth Magic. His Volkhv Magic Resistance is his Conviction, 3 more at noon and 3 less at midnight; in Communion it adds the aura, and his Communion Total against fire, heat and Ignem; he takes the better of it or his Parma, not both. Nastassia found his swallow heart-beast. Bad teeth, a limp. Shortspear, round shield and a fur hauberk. The book prints no Confidence for him.

He has learned enough Latin and theory to be a magus of Ex Miscellanea. A new god is a foolish idea, he thinks, which the gods will find amusing; yet Nastassia found his swallow heart-beast, and Stenya's preaching has begun to convince him. He may seek a great Prophecy.

He lives among the camps and villages and takes no part in the research or the preaching. In 1214 he made the Tribunal give Malincka a hearing without endorsing her; in 1217 he held the Great Cavern and drove off Casimi Ljech, yet he would not lay charges at Crintera. He defends his sodales' rights but will not punish Bjornaer.

After his Gauntlet he fled, rode a year with the Cumans, and in Great Bulgar spent six years studying theology, medicine and philosophy with the scholar Haroun Hashemi, recovering his youthful zest. He met Malincka in 1209 and joined in 1211; outgoing and genial, he is her chief theoretical partner. Nastassia's lover; she is sure he has a deeply buried heart-beast.

She could not read Latin when she came ten years ago and still finds communal life hard. Friend of every local animal, she hates Pripet Maior above all for the raid's harm to them.

characters.name: Yellina Ozwry

description.biography:
Otter heart-beast, battle-worthy, its shape hidden. Afflictions: a limp, failing sight, deafness (she reads lips by a minor InCo spell), dementia and long-term memory loss; her dementia counts against her in spontaneous magic and in controlling a Twilight. A Twilight gave her Clumsy Magic and the next turned it to Chaotic Magic; she is near Final Twilight. The book has her know every listed Animal spell and every listed MuCo, InCo, MuHe and MuAq spell, and any formulaic her Technique + Form beats by ten levels, casting level 10 and less spontaneously.

characters.summary: The covenant's leader, which means only that she is the most lucid of its magi; otter heart-beast. Deaf these five years, she reads lips with a small spell. She is ever surer that her parens Roslav Lavickovich, dead nearly fifty years, still watches over them from Crintera. Stubbornly conservative, she would avoid a fight herself but sees nothing wrong in attacking mundanes, and thinks Thousand Caves a hideous betrayal. Close to Final Twilight, with magic gone chaotic, she is wary with it.

characters.summary: An osprey, who came from Bavaria nearly a century ago and joined Pripet after his Gauntlet at Crintera, when it was at its height. His memory of the present fails, and a dozen times a day he sees the covenant 'suddenly' in ruins, which can bring on fits. A watchful, aggressive sentinel, he strikes interlopers as an Avenging osprey or with storms, and steals what the covenant needs from distant towns, shrunk by magic. A bad Twilight took his Gentle Gift; he now disturbs the beasts he loves, and it eats at him.

characters.summary: The most plainly dangerous: a big, blustering Pole whose water-ox heart-beast leaves him almost no reason, and who shifts without warning between his forms and may stick in one. His longevity potion failed three years ago and he cannot brew another; he ages and has a few years left, and his next Twilight will be his last. He led the raid of 1217 and almost killed Nastassia, and ignores every summons from Three Lakes and Crintera. He prowls the marsh as an ox, terrorizing villagers and fighting its beasts and faeries, magic resistant and very strong: a Twilight made his Form of the Avenging Beast permanent. About a year younger than Miya.

characters.summary: A heron, and by a year the eldest magus of the Tribunal, so its Praeco by the rule (the book names none). Her mind is sounder than Casimi's but her body fails; she rarely leaves her reed palace, the soundest building on the island, and spends her waning power on it. It is a menagerie of waterfowl, beaver, otter, snake, lizard and water-deer, none caged, kept at peace by her great ReAn spell; the beasts, larger and cleverer after generations there, will defend her. A sweet, ancient lady without malice, lost in the world beyond her marsh, and the likeliest host for a Redcap. Zashya Miyovna's mother and parens.

Mounting paranoia makes the whole world a threat; he talks with every visitor and ambushes any he judges dangerous as they leave the marsh. At heart a coward: hard resistance makes him flee, and cornered he is easily cowed.

characters.name: Stanis Chechenko

His patron is the Count of Leczyca. A stooped back, rheumatism, fretful bouts. A Twilight turned his minor Creo deficiency major. His lance, longsword and dagger carry an enhanced Razor's Edge (Damage +6), his shield and half chain mail subtle ReTe spells that lighten them. The book has him master every listed spell of Rego and Perdo with Corpus and Mentem, for political influence and battlefield destruction.

He keeps Leczyca's links strong, visits the courts of lesser nobles (keeping, it seems, the ruling on royalty), guides its merchant ventures, and longs to matter in the Order, writing tirelessly to undermine the Rhine. Some say Leczyca owes its freedom to its walls, not to him. He fears cats.

Kasina's magic is wild and spontaneous and formulaic magic hard for her. Flamboyant, fey and a wicked practical joker, she outrages staid magi and applauds Thousand Caves; she cares for faerie and for her sister. She favours the bow.

She backs Stanis except when trying to take his place, keeps Ruprecht in check, and tries to bring order to the covenant. She long ago reclaimed her sigil. No one has yet beaten her at certamen.

characters.summary: The eldest at Leczyca, who claims authority by it without real ambition. An artisan and enchanter who arms his sodales and the grogs, and one of the makers of the Hermes Portal. In youth he made ornaments and insignia for the Polish royal house, and wept a week when the Order destroyed them and all memory of them. Irritable and bent by his years in the laboratory, still joyful in making, he goes to Verdi every few years for the contests.

characters.name: Yannes Kolski

description.biography:
Afflictions: dementia, a limp, trouble speaking and greater trouble understanding speech, epilepsy. His longevity potion has failed. His great Twilight of 1206 gave him Unpredictable and Painful Magic; he has not worked magic since, and the storyguide may make it useless or wholly uncontrollable. The book has him master every listed spell of Intellego and Muto with Corpus, Imaginem, Mentem and Vim. Visions 8 has no Ability now; the Virtue stays.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 127 as printed; Twilight Points 23 / 3 = Warping 7; Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 0. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.
Virtues and Flaws: Great Intelligence as Great Intelligence; Knack with Enigma as Affinity with Enigmatic Wisdom; Poor Communication as Poor Communication; Sense of Doom dropped (not in the catalog).
Abilities: Brawling 2 to Brawl; Certamen 4 to Penetration; Disputatio 6 to Teaching; Hermes Lore 6 to Organization Lore: Order of Hermes; Hermetic Law 3 to Code of Hermes; Occult Lore 4 to Infernal Lore; Scribe Latin 6 to Artes Liberales; Theology 4 to Theology: Christian; Visions 8 to Premonitions.

characters.summary:
The Mad Magus of the East, a Criamon of Leczyca and master of the Enigma, prone all his life to prophetic visions and small Twilights. In 1206, at 113, he spent two weeks or more in Twilight prophesying; Leczyca's notes of it, the Yannes Discourse, are an apocalyptic morass of verse, cipher, tongues he did not know, and pages where the scribes could only write 'screaming'. One passage is widely known: a black serpent born in the northern fells that breaks the wall of Cathay, burns the Muslims' lands and turns toward him as he flies up, a dove, into Heaven.

He never cast a spell again, but recovered enough to walk and talk, and for ten years went from covenant to covenant, and to the Cumans, reciting that passage with fits, weeping and howling. In 1214 the Quaesitores were asked whether he had passed into Final Twilight and should be restrained; before they decided he vanished, in 1216, near Vladimir-in-Suzdalia, after a disruptive visit to Thousand Caves. His chair at Leczyca stands empty.

pavel_chedyav.name: Pavel Chedyav
pavel_chedyav.summary: Senior, the junior Quaesitor and Andrei's evident successor, which pleases him. An ingenious magus and a fine laboratory worker, he sees the Thousand Caves debate as an intellectual puzzle. He came from Leczyca about fifty years ago, leans to Poland, wants the Polish realm reunited and the Tribunal moved out of Russia, and resents the Royal Embargo though he keeps it. He helped Nicollo make the Eye of Magic.

georgi_yurivich.name: Georgi Yurivich
georgi_yurivich.summary: Senior, Yury's son, apprentice and heir, with magic much like his father's. For thirty years he has run the trading journeys, often in Ladoga and Novgorod or on the northern trails meeting agents and informants. He found and named the Valley of a Thousand Caves more than forty years ago and led Malincka there in 1182; she is his friend, and her work now troubles him. Having aged too little for the mundanes who know him, he wears an enhanced Disguise of the New Visage and turns awkward questions aside with Mentem.

susan_of_wicklow.name: Susan of Wicklow
susan_of_wicklow.summary: Senior and chief Redcap of the Tribunal, that rare thing a Gifted Mercere, of the line of Patrick of Dunderry, whose Russian students died out sixty years ago. One of the age's great travellers: she went with Sadko the merchant in the 1160s and 1170s, later with Georgi into the east, from Sweden to Constantinople. Every year she makes a full circuit of the covenants without the portal, to keep it hidden, coming home by the Leap of Homecoming. Apolitical, proud of the Redcaps. She says she saw Stolitzya about fifteen years ago. Apprentice: Dankya Yostovna.

olga_deiaslavl.name: Olga Deiaslavl
olga_deiaslavl.summary: Specialist, wholly taken up with the Slavic faeries; it is doubtful whether her loyalty is to the covenant or to them, and she is the likeliest to leave, by Twilight, age or Arcadia. A famous teacher, generous on Faerie Lore and Etiquette, her summae and questions the library's pride, but secretive about her spells. Rumour says she has solved faerie time, can wipe away fatigue, and siphons Might from friendly faeries. She is dismissive of Thousand Caves. Apprentice: Kassim ibn Fadal.

boris_davidovich.name: Boris Davidovich
boris_davidovich.summary: Specialist, the youngest magus, Zashya's filius, with a bear heart-beast; a bad Twilight twenty years ago left him huge and covered in wiry brown hair. He believes animals have legends that may hold the wisdom of the world before man, has sought beast lords in Arcadia and griffins, chimeras, pegasi and unicorns in the wild, and records all he finds. He would not join the delegation, though he went with Zashya to Crintera.

nicollo_parelli.name: Nicollo Parelli
nicollo_parelli.summary: Specialist, brought from the Roman Tribunal nearly seventy-five years ago when the council wanted a Verditius; fat, easygoing and fond of his comforts, famed for ingenious laboratory work, and able to lure even proud Pavel into assisting him. Untested in violence or politics, he is beginning to feel he must speak: drawn to Thousand Caves' experiment, yet in sympathy with the vis-hungry western Tribunals. He made Andrei's cloak and Zashya's.

lelya_danichev.name: Lelya Danichev
lelya_danichev.summary: Rehamchi's daughter, a Volkhv raised among the magi, firmer in Hermetic method than her father and keener on Malincka's project; stepmother to Stenya. Impatient to make her mark, she will move at the next meeting that the Tribunal condemn the Order's attitude to the Volkhvy, and wants revenge for the raid: she has practised certamen for three years to force a formal apology from Pripet Maior.

basyl_karrimichi.name: Basyl Karrimichi
basyl_karrimichi.summary: A frivolous prankster with many faerie friends, who will not take research or study seriously; the least use to Malincka. Only his visions sober him: intense and exhausting, they strike at the peak or trough of his seasonally cycling magic, and for five years they have shown the coming of Hermes, so baroque that no one can read them.

otto_rattstein.name: Otto Rattstein
otto_rattstein.summary: An enigma: an elderly Bjornaer of the lynx, once of standing at Crintera, who arrived a little over ten years ago and was admitted though suspected of being a spy. He lives among the camps and villages and takes no part in the research or the preaching. In 1214 he made the Tribunal give Malincka a hearing without endorsing her; in 1217 he held the Great Cavern and drove off Casimi Ljech, yet he would not lay charges at Crintera. He defends his sodales' rights but will not punish Bjornaer.

yakim_ibn_rassur.name: Yakim ibn Rassur
yakim_ibn_rassur.summary: Born in Great Bulgar, sold to Greek merchants as a child and found Gifted in Constantinople by a notoriously cruel Theban Flambeau, whose welts he still bears. After his Gauntlet he fled, rode a year with the Cumans, and in Great Bulgar spent six years studying theology, medicine and philosophy with the scholar Haroun Hashemi, recovering his youthful zest. He met Malincka in 1209 and joined in 1211; outgoing and genial, he is her chief theoretical partner. Nastassia's lover; she is sure he has a deeply buried heart-beast.

narina_cheminov.name: Narina Cheminov
narina_cheminov.summary: Stolen at six by her parens, a very old Bjornaer of the horse who lived his last twenty-five years as a hermit in the Urals, and taught by him from fifteen; her Hermetic magic is eccentric, poor at Penetration, Finesse and certamen, strong in animals, the wild and healing. She could not read Latin when she came ten years ago and still finds communal life hard. Friend of every local animal, she hates Pripet Maior above all for the raid's harm to them.

vlachs_von_hasstein.name: Vlachs von Hasstein
vlachs_von_hasstein.summary: An osprey, who came from Bavaria nearly a century ago and joined Pripet after his Gauntlet at Crintera, when it was at its height. His memory of the present fails, and a dozen times a day he sees the covenant 'suddenly' in ruins, which can bring on fits. A watchful, aggressive sentinel, he strikes interlopers as an Avenging osprey or with storms, and steals what the covenant needs from distant towns, shrunk by magic. A bad Twilight took his Gentle Gift; he now disturbs the beasts he loves, and it eats at him.

casimi_ljech.name: Casimi Ljech
casimi_ljech.summary: The most plainly dangerous: a big, blustering Pole whose water-ox heart-beast leaves him almost no reason, and who shifts without warning between his forms and may stick in one. His longevity potion failed three years ago and he cannot brew another; he ages and has a few years left, and his next Twilight will be his last. He led the raid of 1217 and almost killed Nastassia, and ignores every summons from Three Lakes and Crintera. He prowls the marsh as an ox, terrorizing villagers and fighting its beasts and faeries, magic resistant and very strong: a Twilight made his Form of the Avenging Beast permanent. About a year younger than Miya.

miya_cossuri.name: Miya Cossuri
miya_cossuri.summary: A heron, and by a year the eldest magus of the Tribunal, so its Praeco by the rule (the book names none). Her mind is sounder than Casimi's but her body fails; she rarely leaves her reed palace, the soundest building on the island, and spends her waning power on it. It is a menagerie of waterfowl, beaver, otter, snake, lizard and water-deer, none caged, kept at peace by her great ReAn spell; the beasts, larger and cleverer after generations there, will defend her. A sweet, ancient lady without malice, lost in the world beyond her marsh, and the likeliest host for a Redcap. Zashya Miyovna's mother and parens.

lev_deniki.name: Lev Deniki
lev_deniki.summary: A water serpent, and the deadliest of them behind a pleasant, moderate mask. Mounting paranoia makes the whole world a threat; he talks with every visitor and ambushes any he judges dangerous as they leave the marsh. At heart a coward: hard resistance makes him flee, and cornered he is easily cowed.

kasina_popovich.name: Kasina Popovich
kasina_popovich.summary: One of Gifted twins whose magic is bound together: at a hundred paces apart it is as normal, and it strengthens as they come closer and weakens as they part, by about a point in twenty paces up to five, a Virtue and Flaw together like Cyclic Magic; they have even had the same Twilights at once. Kasina's magic is wild and spontaneous and formulaic magic hard for her. Flamboyant, fey and a wicked practical joker, she outrages staid magi and applauds Thousand Caves; she cares for faerie and for her sister. She favours the bow.

frania_popovich.name: Frania Popovich
frania_popovich.summary: Kasina's twin and opposite: a reserved, dignified, forthright Tremere who respects rank, rules and planning, a student of human law who fights close when she must, and cannot cast spontaneous magic. She backs Stanis except when trying to take his place, keeps Ruprecht in check, and tries to bring order to the covenant. She long ago reclaimed her sigil. No one has yet beaten her at certamen.

tomaszi_klimowicz.name: Tomaszi Klimowicz
tomaszi_klimowicz.summary: The eldest at Leczyca, who claims authority by it without real ambition. An artisan and enchanter who arms his sodales and the grogs, and one of the makers of the Hermes Portal. In youth he made ornaments and insignia for the Polish royal house, and wept a week when the Order destroyed them and all memory of them. Irritable and bent by his years in the laboratory, still joyful in making, he goes to Verdi every few years for the contests.

ruprecht_de_solange.name: Ruprecht de Solange
ruprecht_de_solange.summary: The covenant's baby, a French noble who came forty years ago to harden his will. He idealizes the knight, leads the turb, and enjoys Leczyca's friction, yet chafes that he cannot impose order; the first step is beating Frania at certamen, which he has not managed. He reclaimed his sigil fifteen years ago. Apprentice: Janek.

sanya_tianowicz.name: Sanya Tianowicz
sanya_tianowicz.summary: The covenant's one Bjornaer, a badger, 'recommended' by Crintera's elders fifty years ago: Leczyca feels surer of Crintera with a Bjornaer in residence, though she seems unaware of it. Stable, steadfast in a fight, loyal and resolute, a badger in her home's defence; she joins no faction and cares for the local animals and the covenant's horses.

barchek_ocowski.name: Barchek Ocowski
barchek_ocowski.summary: The Tribunal's other Redcap, unGifted, who relies on devices the Leczycan magi made for him. His routes run west: several Rhine covenants a year (with challenges or rebukes), the Transylvanian covenants of the northern Carpathians, and once a year Rome, with messages for Verdi and complaints for Magvillus. A lean, spry man of peasant stock, funny and tireless, who melts into any stream of travellers.
